def-reg-elastic-net.title: Elastic net
def-reg-elastic-net.html:
For λ1,λ2≥0, the elastic net criterion is Q(b)=12‖y−Xb‖2+λ1‖b‖1+12λ2‖b‖2,{#eq-reg-enet}

and its minimizer 𝛃β^en is the (naive) elastic net estimate. An equivalent parameterization is λ1=αλ, λ2=(1−α)λ, with a mixing parameter α∈[0,1] and an overall level λ≥0.

def-reg-group-lasso.title: Group lasso
def-reg-group-lasso.html:
For weights wg>0, the group lasso criterion is Q(b)=12‖y−∑g=1GXgbg‖2+λ∑g=1Gwg‖bg‖,{#eq-reg-group-lasso}

with Euclidean norms ‖bg‖, not squared. The usual weights are wg=pg. The columns of each group are usually centred and orthonormalized within the group before fitting, so that Xg⊤Xg=Ipg. Different groups are not made orthogonal to each other.

def-reg-l2boost.title: Componentwise L_2 boosting
def-reg-l2boost.title_html: Componentwise L2 boosting
def-reg-l2boost.html:
Fix a step size ν∈(0,2). Start from b(0)=0 and r(0)=y. For m=0,1,2,…:

  1. choose jm=argmaxj(xj⊤r(m))2/‖xj‖2, the column whose simple regression fits the current residual best;
  2. set bjm(m+1)=bjm(m)+νxjm⊤r(m)/‖xjm‖2, leave the other coordinates unchanged, and put r(m+1)=y−Xb(m+1).

The estimate after m steps is b(m), and the stopping iteration m is the tuning parameter.

def-reg-penalized.title: Penalized least squares
def-reg-penalized.html:
A penalty is a function P:Rp→[0,∞). For λ≥0, the penalized least squares criterion is Qλ(b)=12‖y−Xb‖2+λP(b),{#eq-reg-pls}

and a penalized least squares estimate is any minimizer 𝛃β^λ of Qλ. The penalty is convex if P(αb+(1−α)c)≤αP(b)+(1−α)P(c) for all b,c and α∈(0,1), and strictly convex if the inequality is strict whenever b≠c. The penalization is partial if b=(b1⊤,b2⊤)⊤ and P depends on b2 alone; the coefficients in b1 are then unpenalized.

def-reg-stagewise.title: Incremental forward stagewise regression
def-reg-stagewise.html: Fix ε>0. Start from b(0)=0. At step k, with residual r(k)=y−Xb(k), choose j=argmaxj|xj⊤r(k)| and set bj(k+1)=bj(k)+εsign(xj⊤r(k)), leaving the other coordinates unchanged. Write FSε for this procedure, and FS0 for the limit of its paths as ε→0, when the limit exists.

def-reg-subgradient.title: Subgradient
def-reg-subgradient.html: Let P be convex. A vector s is a subgradient of P at b if P(c)≥P(b)+s⊤(c−b) for every c∈Rp. The set of all subgradients at b is the subdifferential ∂P(b).

eq-reg-block-soft.html: 𝛃β^g=(1−λwg‖zg‖)+zg.

eq-reg-boost-drop.html: Q(b(m))−Q(b(m+1))=ν(1−ν2)maxj(xj⊤r(m))2‖xj‖2;

eq-reg-boost-operator.html: Bm=I−(I−νHjm−1)⋯(I−νHj0),Hj=xjxj⊤‖xj‖2,

eq-reg-cd.html: bj=sign(xj⊤r(j))(|xj⊤r(j)|−λ1)+‖xj‖2+λ2.

eq-reg-enet.html: Q(b)=12‖y−Xb‖2+λ1‖b‖1+12λ2‖b‖2,

eq-reg-enet-kkt.html: 𝛃𝛃xj⊤(y−Xβ^)−λ2β^j=λ1sign(β^j)  (β^j≠0),|xj⊤(y−Xβ^)|≤λ1  (β^j=0).

eq-reg-expansion.html: 𝛃𝛃Qλ(b)−Qλ(β^)=−d⊤X⊤r+12‖Xd‖2+λ(P(b)−P(β^)).

eq-reg-fused.html: Q(b)=12‖y−Xb‖2+λ1∑j=1p|bj|+λ2∑j=2p|bj−bj−1|.

eq-reg-group-kkt.html: 𝛃𝛃𝛃𝛃Xg⊤r=λwgβ^g‖β^g‖if β^g≠0,‖Xg⊤r‖≤λwgif β^g=0.

eq-reg-group-lasso.html: Q(b)=12‖y−∑g=1GXgbg‖2+λ∑g=1Gwg‖bg‖,

eq-reg-grouping.html: 𝛃|β^i−β^j|≤‖y−Xβ^‖‖xi−xj‖λ2≤‖y‖2(1−ρij)λ2.

eq-reg-kkt.html: 𝛃𝛃X⊤(y−Xβ^)∈λ∂P(β^).

eq-reg-lasso-segment.html: 𝛃β^A(λ)=(XA⊤XA)−1(XA⊤y−λsA),

eq-reg-pls.html: Qλ(b)=12‖y−Xb‖2+λP(b),

eq-reg-rescaled.html: 12c⊤Σλ2c−y⊤Xc+λ1‖c‖1,Σλ2=X⊤X+λ2I1+λ2.

exm-reg-boosting.title: Boosting a sparse regression
exm-reg-boosting.html:
The script draws n=60 observations of p=30 normal regressors with correlations 0.5|j−k|, five nonzero coefficients and σ=1.5, and boosts on the standardized regressors. The expected squared error on a new case (the risk) is computed exactly from the design law; its floor is σ2=2.25.

Convergence. For ν=0.1, κ=3.18×10−4, and 𝛃𝛃‖b(m)−β^‖/‖β^‖ is 0.497, 0.161 and 2.7×10−8 after 100, 1000 and 50000 steps; the script checks @eq-reg-boost-drop and the bound (b) at every step.

Early stopping. Least squares has risk 4.046. With ν=0.1 the risk is smallest, 2.981, after 108 steps (with 14 nonzero coefficients), and within 5 per cent of that from m=72 to m=305; five-fold cross-validation chooses m=229, with risk 3.047. With ν=1 the best risk, 2.893, occurs at m=4 and only there is the risk within 5 per cent of it: a needle that a data-based stopping rule is unlikely to hit (Figure 30.4.1).

Degrees of freedom. Over 2000 responses with the same design and mean, the covariance degrees of freedom after m=20 steps are 3.1 against an average trace of 1.5, and after m=120 steps 12.6 against 6.2. The trace does not see the adaptation of the chosen columns to the noise.

exm-reg-factors.title: Selecting factors
exm-reg-factors.html: The script simulates n=120 observations of four factors A,B,C,D (with 4, 3, 5 and 3 levels) and three numeric regressors; the response depends on A, weakly on B, and on x1. The group lasso path starts at λmax=6.876, and groups enter in the order x1, A, B, D. At λ=2.0 only A and x1 are selected, with 𝛃‖XAβ^A‖=2.834 and 𝛃‖Xx1β^x1‖=4.861. Another reference level gives the same fitted contributions to machine precision. The lasso on the raw indicator columns does not: at λ=6.0 its fit moves by 8.6 per cent of its length when the reference levels change. Along its path the columns of A enter at values of λ spread over a factor of 2.8, and it admits its first column of a null factor (C or D) at a residual sum of squares of 112.0, a worse fit than the 110.7 that the group lasso reaches with both null factors still excluded (Figure 30.3.1).

exm-reg-grouping.title: Three near-copies of one signal
exm-reg-grouping.html:
The script simulates n=50 observations of p=10 regressors. The first three are noisy copies of a common variable, with pairwise correlations between 0.93 and 0.95, and each has coefficient 2 (on the unit-length scale). The other seven are independent noise. With λ1=0.8:

β^1 β^2 β^3 nonzero
lasso (λ2=0) 2.335 0.000 2.522 2
elastic net (λ2=1) 1.248 1.103 1.236 4
rescaled elastic net 2.496 2.207 2.471 4

The lasso drops the second copy. The elastic net keeps all three with similar coefficients (and one noise regressor, at 0.081). For the pair (1,2), with correlation 0.927, the spread 0.144 is well inside @eq-reg-grouping, whose middle term is 1.577 (residual norm 4.129) and right-hand side 2.532 (‖y‖=6.630). Along the lasso path (Figure 30.2.1) the second copy enters only after λ has fallen by a factor of about 26; along the elastic net path all three enter at the same grid value.

exm-reg-laplace-mean.title: Posterior mode and posterior mean under a Laplace prior
exm-reg-laplace-mean.title_html: Posterior mode and posterior mean under a Laplace prior
exm-reg-laplace-mean.html:
Take one observation z∼N(θ,1) and a Laplace prior on θ with rate a=1.5. By @prp-reg-map(b) the posterior mode is the lasso estimate with λ=1.5, which is soft thresholding at 1.5 (@thm-shr-lasso-orthonormal). The posterior mean, computed by numerical integration in the listing below, behaves differently:

z 0.5 1.0 2.0 4.0
posterior mode 0 0 0.500 2.500
posterior mean 0.174 0.364 0.859 2.509

The mode is zero for |z|≤1.5; the mean is zero only at z=0, and approaches z−1.5 for large z (Figure 30.1.1(c)). Exact zeros come from the mode, not from the prior; a prior that believes in exact zeros needs a point mass, as in the spike-and-slab priors of George and McCulloch (1993). Chapter 39 returns to priors as regularizers.

exm-reg-stagewise.title: Stagewise and lasso paths
exm-reg-stagewise.html:
Orthonormal design. With 5 orthonormal columns and ε=0.01, the largest distance from the lasso estimate at λ=τk over all steps is 0.0092.

A non-monotone lasso path. For n=40 observations of p=6 regressors sharing a common factor (correlations near 0.64), the lasso coefficient of regressor 6 grows to 0.308 at ‖b‖1=4.12 and then shrinks back. FSε with ε=0.002 agrees with the lasso to within 0.039 until then, and afterwards holds the coefficient: halfway to the least squares norm 7.53, the two differ by 0.165 there (Figure 30.5.1). At every ℓ1 norm checked, the lasso has the smaller residual sum of squares, as it must; the excess of stagewise is at most 0.011.

Prediction. Over 50 data sets from the design of @exm-reg-boosting, the average smallest risk along the path is 2.857 for the lasso, 2.857 for stagewise and 2.856 for boosting with ν=0.05, against 4.607 for least squares. Data set by data set the points lie close to the diagonal (panel (c)): the best risks of stagewise and boosting never differ from the lasso’s by more than 6.6 per cent.

exr-reg-arc-length.title: A2
exr-reg-arc-length.html: Show that the ℓ1 arc length of the FSε path after k steps is kε, that it is at least ‖b(k)‖1, and that equality holds iff no coordinate has ever moved in both directions. Which of the two paths in Figure 30.5.1 has equality up to the least squares region?

exr-reg-boost-df-orthonormal.title: C1
exr-reg-boost-df-orthonormal.html: Under an orthonormal design with 𝛃y∼Nn(Xβ,σ2I), the lasso fit with parameter λ has covariance degrees of freedom E#{j:|zj|>λ} (by Stein’s lemma, @lem-shr-stein, applied coordinatewise). Show that hard thresholding at the same λ has covariance degrees of freedom E#{j:|zj|>λ}+∑j(λ/σ){ϕ((λ−βj)/σ)+ϕ((λ+βj)/σ)}, where ϕ is the standard normal density. The extra term is the price of selecting without shrinking.

exr-reg-boost-drop-sum.title: B1
exr-reg-boost-drop-sum.html: Use @eq-reg-boost-drop to show that ∑m≥0maxj(xj⊤r(m))2/‖xj‖2≤‖y‖2/{ν(2−ν)}. Deduce, without the singular value argument, that X⊤r(m)→0 for every ν∈(0,2).

exr-reg-boost-orthonormal-step.title: A1
exr-reg-boost-orthonormal-step.html: Let X⊤X=I, z=X⊤y=(3,−1,0.5)⊤ and ν=0.1. Carry out the first three boosting steps by hand. Show that under an orthonormal design the current residual correlations are z−b(m), so boosting always moves the coordinate whose remaining correlation is largest in absolute value, and removes one tenth of that correlation.

exr-reg-boost-soft.title: B1
exr-reg-boost-soft.html: Adapt the proof of @prp-reg-stagewise-orthonormal to componentwise boosting with step ν∈(0,1] under an orthonormal design. Show that τk is nonincreasing and that |bj(k)−sign(zj)(|zj|−τk)+|≤ντk for all j and k.

exr-reg-en-identical.title: B2
exr-reg-en-identical.html: Let X=[x,x] with ‖x‖=1. Find the elastic net estimate in closed form and compare it with the ridge and lasso estimates.

exr-reg-en-orthonormal.title: A1
exr-reg-en-orthonormal.html: Under an orthonormal design with z=X⊤y=(3,0.5,−1.2)⊤, λ1=1 and λ2=1, compute the lasso, ridge, naive elastic net and rescaled elastic net estimates.

exr-reg-firm-continuous.title: A2
exr-reg-firm-continuous.html: Show that the firm thresholding rule ϕ of @prp-reg-mcp(b) is continuous at |z|=λ and at |z|=γλ, whereas the hard thresholding rule z1(|z|>λ) jumps by λ at |z|=λ. What is the largest slope of ϕ, and what happens to it as γ↓1?

exr-reg-fs-hand.title: A1
exr-reg-fs-hand.html: Let X⊤X=I, z=(3,−1,0.5)⊤ and ε=0.5. Run FSε by hand until the largest absolute residual correlation first falls below 1, and check @prp-reg-stagewise-orthonormal(b) at each step.

exr-reg-fs-two.title: B3
exr-reg-fs-two.html: Show that for p=2 (unit-length columns, correlation ρ∈(−1,1)) the direction dA always has the signs sA. Conclude, using @prp-reg-stagewise(b), that FS0 and the lasso path coincide for every data set with two regressors.

exr-reg-fused-two.title: B1
exr-reg-fused-two.html: Solve the fused lasso @eq-reg-fused with X=I2, λ1=0 and λ2=λ. Show that β^1=β^2=12(y1+y2) if |y1−y2|≤2λ. Otherwise, each estimate moves a distance λ from its observation towards the other.

exr-reg-group-nonorthonormal.title: C1
exr-reg-group-nonorthonormal.html: Drop the assumption Xg⊤Xg=I. Show that a nonzero solution of the block problem minb12‖r−Xgb‖2+c‖b‖ is b=(Xg⊤Xg+(c/t)I)−1Xg⊤r, where t=‖b‖ is the root of a one-dimensional equation. Show that this equation has a unique root when ‖Xg⊤r‖>c, so the block update is a ridge regression (@thm-shr-ridge) with a data-dependent parameter.

exr-reg-group-vs-lasso.title: B2
exr-reg-group-vs-lasso.html: Under an orthonormal design, compare the group lasso (one group of size 3, w=3) with the lasso on the same three columns, for z=(2,0.3,−0.2)⊤ and λ=1. Which coefficients are zero in each? Show that, under an orthonormal design, the group lasso never sets a single coordinate of a selected group to zero unless the corresponding zj=0.

exr-reg-group-weights.title: A1
exr-reg-group-weights.html: Under orthonormal groups and y∼Nn(0,σ2I), show that 𝛃P(β^g≠0)=P{χ2(pg)>λ2wg2/σ2}. With wg=1, compare these probabilities for pg=1 and pg=10 when λ=2σ. What do the weights pg achieve, and what do they not achieve?

exr-reg-grouping-opposite.title: B1
exr-reg-grouping-opposite.html: Show that if β^iβ^j<0, then |β^i+β^j|≤‖y‖2(1+ρij)/λ2. Interpret this for two regressors with correlation close to −1.

exr-reg-intercept.title: B2
exr-reg-intercept.html: Let P be any penalty on the slopes, and let the model have an unpenalized intercept. By @prp-shr-centring, 𝛃(b^0,β^) minimizes 12∑i(yi−b0−x(i)⊤b)2+λP(b) iff 𝛃β^ minimizes the centred criterion and 𝛃b^0=y¯−x¯⊤β^. Deduce that the fitted values of penalized regression with an intercept are unchanged when a constant is added to y, and that the slopes are unchanged when a constant is added to a column of X. Does the second statement survive standardizing the columns before fitting?

exr-reg-landweber.title: B2
exr-reg-landweber.html: For the gradient descent iteration of @prp-reg-boosting-operator(d) with 0<ν<2/σ12, show that every b(m) lies in C(X⊤), and that b(m)→X+y, the minimum-norm least squares estimate (@prp-proj-min-norm). Why does this argument fail for componentwise boosting?

exr-reg-lars-breakpoints.title: B2
exr-reg-lars-breakpoints.html: On a segment of the lasso path with active set A and signs sA, show that the correlation of an inactive regressor is cj(λ)=xj⊤(I−MA)y+λxj⊤XA(XA⊤XA)−1sA, where MA projects onto C(XA). Deduce the value of λ at which j joins the active set, and the value at which an active coefficient reaches zero. This is the lasso version of least angle regression.

exr-reg-lasso-at-most-n.title: C1
exr-reg-lasso-at-most-n.html: Suppose p>n and the lasso estimate 𝛃β^ is unique with active set A. Use the KKT conditions to show that the columns XA are linearly independent, and deduce that |A|≤n. (Hint: if XAd=0 with d≠0, move along 𝛃β^+τ(d,0) and use that the fit and the ℓ1 norm are constant among minimizers.)

exr-reg-mcp-nonconvex.title: C1
exr-reg-mcp-nonconvex.html: Let n=p=2, X⊤X=(1rr1) with r∈(0,1), and use MCP with γ>1. For which r does @prp-reg-mcp(a) guarantee convexity? Find a response y for which the MCP criterion has two distinct local minima when r exceeds that bound.

exr-reg-rules.title: A1
exr-reg-rules.html: With λ=1, compute the lasso, ridge (penalty 12b2), hard, firm (γ=3) and SCAD (a=3.7) estimates of θ for a single observation z=2.5 under an orthonormal design. Which rules shrink it, and by how much?

exr-reg-scad.title: B1
exr-reg-scad.html: Derive the SCAD thresholding rule displayed above. Minimize g(θ)=12(z−θ)2+ρ(θ) for z≥0 on the three pieces [0,λ], [λ,aλ] and [aλ,∞), and check that g is convex on [0,∞) when a>2.

lem-reg-norm-subgradient.title: Subdifferential of a sum of block norms
lem-reg-norm-subgradient.title_html: Subdifferential of a sum of block norms
lem-reg-norm-subgradient.html: Let G1,…,GK partition {1,…,p}, let w1,…,wK>0, and let P(b)=∑kwk‖bGk‖, where bGk is the subvector of b with coordinates in Gk. Then s∈∂P(b) iff, for every k, sGk=wkbGk‖bGk‖if bGk≠0,‖sGk‖≤wkif bGk=0. With singleton blocks and unit weights, P=‖⋅‖1, and s∈∂‖b‖1 iff sj=sign(bj) when bj≠0 and |sj|≤1 when bj=0.

lem-reg-optimality.title: Optimality condition
lem-reg-optimality.html:
Let P be convex and λ>0. A vector 𝛃β^ minimizes Qλ iff 𝛃𝛃X⊤(y−Xβ^)∈λ∂P(β^).{#eq-reg-kkt}

In that case 𝛃𝛃Qλ(b)−Qλ(β^)≥12‖X(b−β^)‖2 for every b.

prp-reg-boosting-operator.title: The boosting operator
prp-reg-boosting-operator.html:
1. f(m)=Bmy with Bm=I−(I−νS)m.

  2. Let S be symmetric with eigenvalues dk≥0 and orthonormal eigenvectors uk, and let νdk≤1 for every k. Then Bm=∑k{1−(1−νdk)m}ukuk⊤. Each factor 1−(1−νdk)m lies in [0,1], is nondecreasing in m, and tends to 1 when dk>0. The trace trBm increases with m towards rankS.

  3. (Least squares learner.) If S=M, then Bm={1−(1−ν)m}M. Early stopping shrinks the least squares fit by a single factor.

  4. (Gradient descent.) The iteration b(m+1)=b(m)+νX⊤(y−Xb(m)) from b(0)=0 is the case S=XX⊤. If X has singular values σk and νσk2≤1, its fitted values shrink the kth singular component of the least squares fit by 1−(1−νσk2)m. Ridge regression shrinks the same component by σk2/(σk2+λ).

prp-reg-coordinate.title: Coordinate update
prp-reg-coordinate.html: Fix all coordinates of b except bj, and let r(j)=y−∑k≠jxkbk be the partial residual. The value of bj that minimizes @eq-reg-enet is bj=sign(xj⊤r(j))(|xj⊤r(j)|−λ1)+‖xj‖2+λ2.{#eq-reg-cd}

prp-reg-elastic-net.title: Elastic net: uniqueness, augmented data, grouping
prp-reg-elastic-net.title_html: Elastic net: uniqueness, augmented data, grouping
prp-reg-elastic-net.html:
Let λ2>0.

  1. The criterion @eq-reg-enet has a unique minimizer, whatever the rank of X. It is characterized by 𝛃𝛃xj⊤(y−Xβ^)−λ2β^j=λ1sign(β^j)  (β^j≠0),|xj⊤(y−Xβ^)|≤λ1  (β^j=0).{#eq-reg-enet-kkt}

  2. (Augmented data.) Let X∗=(Xλ2Ip) and y∗=(y0). Then 𝛃β^en is the lasso estimate, with parameter λ1, for the data (X∗,y∗). The matrix X∗ has full column rank p.

  3. (Orthonormal design.) If X⊤X=I, then β^jen=sign(zj)(|zj|−λ1)+/(1+λ2), with z=X⊤y.

  4. (Grouping effect.) If β^iβ^j>0, then 𝛃|β^i−β^j|≤‖y−Xβ^‖‖xi−xj‖λ2≤‖y‖2(1−ρij)λ2.{#eq-reg-grouping}

  5. (Identical columns.) If xi=xj, then β^i=β^j.

prp-reg-group-invariance.title: Invariance to the coding of a group
prp-reg-group-invariance.title_html: Invariance to the coding of a group
prp-reg-group-invariance.html:
1. Let Ug be pg×pg orthogonal matrices, and replace every Xg by XgUg. Then 𝛃β^ minimizes the original criterion iff the vector with blocks 𝛃Ug⊤β^g minimizes the new one. The fitted contributions 𝛃Xgβ^g are the same.

  2. Suppose each group is orthonormalized within itself, so that Xg is an orthonormal basis of a subspace Vg. Then the minimizers, expressed through the fitted contributions 𝛃Xgβ^g∈Vg, depend on the groups only through the subspaces Vg. In particular, for a factor they do not depend on the choice of reference level or of contrasts.

prp-reg-group-lasso.title: Group lasso and block soft thresholding
prp-reg-group-lasso.title_html: Group lasso and block soft thresholding
prp-reg-group-lasso.html:
1. A minimizer of @eq-reg-group-lasso exists, and all minimizers have the same fitted vector.

  2. (KKT conditions.) 𝛃β^ is a minimizer iff, with 𝛃r=y−Xβ^, for every group g, 𝛃𝛃𝛃𝛃Xg⊤r=λwgβ^g‖β^g‖if β^g≠0,‖Xg⊤r‖≤λwgif β^g=0.{#eq-reg-group-kkt}

  3. Let λ>0. Then 𝛃β^=0 iff λ≥λmax=maxg‖Xg⊤y‖/wg.

  4. (Orthonormal groups.) If Xg⊤Xh=Ipg for g=h and 0 for g≠h, the unique minimizer is block soft thresholding of zg=Xg⊤y: 𝛃β^g=(1−λwg‖zg‖)+zg.{#eq-reg-block-soft}

  5. (Block update; compare @prp-reg-coordinate.) If Xg⊤Xg=Ipg, then minimizing @eq-reg-group-lasso over bg with the other blocks fixed gives @eq-reg-block-soft with zg replaced by sg=Xg⊤r(g), where r(g)=y−∑h≠gXhbh is the partial residual.

prp-reg-map.title: Penalized estimates as posterior modes
prp-reg-map.html:
Let 𝛃Y∼Nn(Xβ,σ2I) with σ2 known, and give 𝛃β a prior density π(b)∝exp⁡{−(λ/σ2)P(b)}, assumed integrable. Then the posterior density of 𝛃β is proportional to exp⁡{−Qλ(b)/σ2}. So the penalized least squares estimates are exactly the posterior modes. In particular:

  1. a normal prior 𝛃β∼Np(0,τ2I) gives ridge regression (@thm-shr-ridge) with λ=σ2/τ2, and the posterior mode equals the posterior mean;

  2. independent Laplace priors with density (a/2)e−a|bj| give the lasso with λ=aσ2.

prp-reg-mcp.title: MCP: convexity and firm thresholding
prp-reg-mcp.html:
Let Q(b)=12‖y−Xb‖2+∑jρ(bj) with ρ the MCP penalty.

  1. If the smallest eigenvalue of X⊤X is at least 1/γ, then Q is convex. If it exceeds 1/γ, then Q is strictly convex and has a unique minimizer.

  2. If X⊤X=I, the unique minimizer is β^j=ϕ(zj) with z=X⊤y, where ϕ is firm thresholding: ϕ(z)={0,|z|≤λ,sign(z)|z|−λ1−1/γ,λ<|z|≤γλ,z,|z|>γλ.

prp-reg-rescaled.title: The rescaled elastic net
prp-reg-rescaled.html: Let the columns of X have unit length and let λ2>0. Then 𝛃𝛃β~=(1+λ2)β^en is the unique minimizer of 12c⊤Σλ2c−y⊤Xc+λ1‖c‖1,Σλ2=X⊤X+λ2I1+λ2.{#eq-reg-rescaled}

prp-reg-stagewise.title: Stagewise and the lasso path
prp-reg-stagewise.html:
1. Suppose that for λ in an interval the lasso estimate is unique and has a fixed active set A and fixed signs sA, and XA has full column rank. Then on that interval 𝛃β^A(λ)=(XA⊤XA)−1(XA⊤y−λsA),{#eq-reg-lasso-segment}

    so as λ decreases the active coefficients move along the direction dA=(XA⊤XA)−1sA, and all active variables keep the common absolute correlation λ with the residual.

  2. (Sketch; Efron, Hastie, Johnstone and Tibshirani, 2004, who prove it under their positive cone condition on the design; Hastie et al., 2007, for monotone paths.) If along the whole lasso path every direction dA has the signs sA coordinatewise, that is, if every lasso coefficient is monotone in λ, then FS0 exists and coincides with the lasso path.

  3. (Sketch; Hastie, Taylor, Tibshirani and Walther, 2007.) In general FS0 is the path of the monotone lasso. Write b=b+−b− with b±≥0. Along the path, every coordinate of b+ and of b− is nondecreasing, and the path lowers the residual sum of squares as fast as possible per unit of ℓ1 arc length, subject to that constraint.

prp-reg-stagewise-orthonormal.title: Stagewise under an orthonormal design
prp-reg-stagewise-orthonormal.html:
Let X⊤X=I, z=X⊤y, and let τk=maxj|zj−bj(k)| be the largest absolute residual correlation after k steps of FSε. Let K be the last step before τ first falls below ε, so that τ0,…,τK≥ε. For every k≤K:

  1. τk+1≤τk (for k<K);

  2. every coordinate satisfies |bj(k)−sign(zj)(|zj|−τk)+|≤ε, that is, FSε is within ε of the lasso estimate at λ=τk.

Consequently, the part of the stagewise path with τk≥ε and the lasso path are within 3ε of each other, in the sense that every point of either is within 3ε of some point of the other in every coordinate. As ε→0 the stagewise path converges to the lasso path.

thm-reg-boosting.title: Convergence of componentwise L_2 boosting
thm-reg-boosting.title_html: Convergence of componentwise L2 boosting
thm-reg-boosting.html:
Let ν∈(0,2), let Q(b)=12‖y−Xb‖2 with minimum Q∗, let s>0 be the smallest nonzero singular value of X, and put κ=ν(2−ν)s2pmaxj‖xj‖2. Then 0<κ≤1, and:

  1. each step lowers the residual sum of squares by exactly Q(b(m))−Q(b(m+1))=ν(1−ν2)maxj(xj⊤r(m))2‖xj‖2;{#eq-reg-boost-drop}

  2. Q(b(m))−Q∗≤(1−κ)m(Q(0)−Q∗). Hence the fitted values converge geometrically to the least squares fit: ‖Xb(m)−My‖2=2{Q(b(m))−Q∗}→0;

  3. the coefficients b(m) converge to a least squares estimate. If X has full column rank, the limit is 𝛃β^.

thm-reg-existence.title: Existence and uniqueness of penalized estimates
thm-reg-existence.title_html: Existence and uniqueness of penalized estimates
thm-reg-existence.html:
Let P be continuous and λ≥0.

  1. If Qλ(b)→∞ as ‖b‖→∞, a minimizer exists. This holds in each of three cases: (i) X has full column rank; (ii) λ>0 and P(b)≥c‖b‖ for some c>0; (iii) the penalization is partial, X=[X1,X2] with X1 of full column rank, λ>0, and P(b)≥c‖b2‖ for some c>0.

  2. If P is convex, the set of minimizers is convex, and all minimizers have the same fitted vector 𝛃Xβ^λ. If in addition λ>0, they all have the same penalty 𝛃P(β^λ).

  3. If P is convex and either X has full column rank, or λ>0 and P is strictly convex, the minimizer is unique.
